dublinCore.dc:title: 119 HR 9913 IH: Safe Sips Act of 2026
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. LaLota introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, and the Secretary of the Treasury, acting through the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau, to establish a system for color coding certain intoxicating drinks, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Safe Sips Act of 2026.

section.header: Color-coding system for certain intoxicating drinks

subsection.text: The Secretary shall establish a system for color coding the packaging of a covered drink that—

paragraph.text: identifies one single color to be used at the dispensing point of such packaging, regardless of the type of intoxicating substance in such drink;

includes a non-color identifier on such packaging, including text, a symbol, a pattern, a tactile feature, or such other identifier, for purposes of ensuring accessibility to a consumer of such drink who is blind or colorblind; and
for purposes of enforcing the prohibition under subsection (b)(4), provides for technical specifications and color tolerances as to the meaning of substantially similar color.

subsection.header: Requirements With respect to implementation of system

paragraph.text: A manufacturer of a covered drink shall implement the system established under subsection (a).
A distributor or retailer shall disseminate information, as determined by the Secretary, to consumers with respect to the system established under subsection (a).
A retailer shall ensure that any covered drink sold, or offered for sale, by such retailer complies with the system established under subsection (a).

paragraph.header: Prohibition on use of color for non-covered drink
paragraph.text: A manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may not include the color identified under subsection (a)(1), or a substantially similar color, at the dispensing point of the packaging of a drink that is not a covered drink.

subsection.text: For purposes of enforcing the requirements under subsection (b), the Secretary shall establish—

paragraph.text: a procedure for assessing a civil penalty on any manufacturer, distributor, or retailer who does not comply with such requirements; and
a structure for determining such a fine.

subsection.text: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall issue such rules as may be necessary to implement this section.

No State, political division of a State, or Tribal government may enact, adopt, promulgate, or enforce any law, regulation, or other requirement that is in addition to, or more stringent than, a requirement or prohibition established under this section.
Nothing in this Act shall be construed to effect—

paragraph.text: the authority under the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 801 et seq.), including the scheduling of a controlled substance or any requirement or prohibition with respect to such scheduling; or

the authority under any other Federal law with respect to the manufacture, distribution, sale, importation, possession, or introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce of a covered drink.
The term alcohol means any drink that—

subparagraph.text: contains not less than 0.05 percent alcohol by volume; and

paragraph.text: The term covered drink means a drink for sale that—

clause.text: a single can or bottle; or
any such other container, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.text: The term covered substance means—

subparagraph.text: any such other intoxicating substance, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.text: The term dispensing point—

subparagraph.text: means the top, end, closure, or such other component of a drink container through which a consumer can access, open, pour, or otherwise dispense such drink; and

includes a can end, bottle cap, bottle closure, lid, cork, stopper, spout, nozzle, spigot, or such other component, as determined by the Secretary, for accessing, opening, pouring, or otherwise dispensing such drink.

paragraph.text: The term distributor—

subparagraph.text: means a person that sells, transfers, or delivers a covered drink for resale; and
does not include a person acting solely as a common carrier.

paragraph.text: The term intoxicating cannabinoid means a cannabinoid, including an isomer, a derivative, an analogue, a homolog, or a synthetic cannabinoid, that has an intoxicating or impairing effect substantially similar to or greater than THC, as determined by the Secretary, when ingested by a human.
The term Kratom-related substance means—

subparagraph.text: Mitragyna speciosa Korth., including any part, extract, preparation, concentrate, alkaloid, constituent, derivative, salt, isomer, or mixture of Mitragyna speciosa Korth.;
7-hydroxymitragynine, including any substance containing enhanced, concentrated, chemically converted, or synthetically produced 7-hydroxymitragynine.

paragraph.text: The term manufacturer means a person that commercially produces, prepares, packages, repackages, labels, relabels, or imports a covered drink for sale or distribution in the United States.

The term retailer means a person to whom a covered drink is delivered or sold, if such delivery or sale is for purposes of sale or distribution in commerce to purchasers who buy such drink for purposes other than resale.
The term Secretary means, as applicable—

subparagraph.text: the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Commissioner of Food and Drugs; and
the Secretary of the Treasury, acting through the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau.

paragraph.text: The term THC means a tetrahydrocannabinol or any isomer thereof, as determined by the Secretary, including a delta-8, delta-9, or delta-10 tetrahydrocannabinol, regardless of whether such tetrahydrocannabinol or isomer is naturally occurring, chemically converted, synthesized, or derived from hemp, marihuana, or any such other source.

subsection.text: This Act shall apply to a covered drink manufactured, distributed, sold, or offered for sale on or after the date that is 4 years after the date of enactment of this Act.
